# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview
The old and new billing systems will run in parallel (dual-run) throughout the migration. Users are moved in batches based on cohort risk (internal/test accounts first, then low-complexity accounts, then the general population, then remaining high-complexity/high-value accounts). The old system remains fully operational as a fallback until all cohorts are validated and a separate, later decommissioning phase is executed.

---

## Phase 1: Internal & Pilot Cohort — 1% of users (~400 users)
**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end QA in staging, including invoice generation, tax calculation, payment retries, and refund flows, with 100% parity against the old system on a replayed sample of at least 5,000 historical transactions. Rollback procedure has been tested and confirmed to restore a user to the old system within 15 minutes.

**Scope:** Internal employee accounts, sandbox accounts, and volunteer beta customers who have opted in.

**Activities:** Full dual-write/dual-read reconciliation enabled; manual review of every invoice generated for this cohort for the first two billing cycles.

---

## Phase 2: Low-Complexity General Availability — 15% of users (~6,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed at least one full billing cycle (typically 30 days) with zero unresolved critical discrepancies, invoice accuracy ≥ 99.95%, and support ticket volume for migrated users within 1.2x of baseline for non-migrated users.

**Scope:** Users on standard/simple plans (single currency, no custom contracts, no multi-entity billing), selected randomly within that segment to avoid selection bias.

**Activities:** Automated reconciliation job compares old vs. new system output for every invoice for the first 14 days post-migration. Customer support briefed and given a rollback runbook.

---

## Phase 3: General Rollout — 60% of users (~24,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 sustained for at least 21 days with invoice accuracy ≥ 99.9%, payment failure rate delta vs. control group ≤ 0.5 percentage points, and no Sev1/Sev2 billing incidents in the prior 14 days. Support team confirms staffing and escalation paths are ready for higher volume.

**Scope:** All remaining standard and mid-complexity accounts (multi-currency, coupons/discounts, mid-tier contracts), migrated in weekly waves of ~6,000 to allow monitoring between waves.

**Activities:** Continued reconciliation on a statistically significant sample (minimum 10% of daily transactions); daily review of financial metrics with finance team.

---

## Phase 4: High-Complexity & Final Batch — 24% of users (~9,600 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with cumulative invoice accuracy ≥ 99.9% across all migrated cohorts, zero open critical billing defects, and sign-off from Finance, Support, and Engineering leads. Dedicated migration support window scheduled with affected enterprise customers.

**Scope:** Enterprise accounts, custom contracts, multi-entity billing, and any accounts requiring white-glove migration with account manager involvement.

**Activities:** White-glove migration with pre- and post-migration invoice comparison sent directly to key accounts; extended 30-day dual-run monitoring for this cohort specifically before this phase is considered closed.

*(Note: Decommissioning of the old billing system is explicitly deferred to a separate, subsequent phase — Phase 5 — occurring only after Phase 4's cohort has completed its full validation window. Phase 4 covers user migration only, not system retirement.)*

---

## Phase 5 (Post-Migration): Legacy System Decommissioning — 0% of users (no user migration in this phase)
**Entry criterion:** All 40,000 users fully migrated and stable on the new system for at least 30 consecutive days with no reopened rollbacks, plus a completed financial audit reconciling old vs. new system totals for the full migration period.

**Activities:** Freeze writes to old system, archive historical data, decommission infrastructure.

---

## Risks

RISK: Invoice calculation discrepancies between old and new systems cause customer billing errors | Run mandatory dual-write reconciliation with automated diffing for every migrated account for at least 14 days post-migration; block phase advancement on any unresolved discrepancy | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Payment gateway integration in the new system fails silently for a subset of payment methods | Implement synthetic transaction monitoring across all supported payment methods every 15 minutes, with automated paging on failure | Payments Platform Engineer
RISK: Data migration scripts corrupt or drop customer payment method/tokenization data | Perform pre-migration and post-migration record counts and checksum validation per batch; require a passing validation report before a batch is marked complete | Data Migration Engineer
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during a phase, delaying resolution and increasing churn risk | Staff a dedicated migration support queue with surge capacity pre-approved for each phase, activated automatically if ticket volume exceeds threshold | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback from new system back to old system is slower or less reliable than expected during an active incident | Rehearse rollback procedure in staging before each phase and require a demonstrated rollback time under 15 minutes as a phase gate | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

---

## Halt Criteria

The rollout will be immediately paused (no further batches migrated) and the current phase's cohort evaluated for rollback if any of the following occurs:
- **Invoice accuracy drops below 99.5%** for any migrated cohort over a rolling 24-hour window.
- Payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds control group by more than **2 percentage points** over a rolling 24-hour window.
- More than **5 Sev1 billing incidents** occur within any single 7-day period attributable to the new system.

PHASES: 5
